doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Reflections and recording 'Daybreak'
summary: Monk's closing thoughts; Al recalls recording 'Daybreak' and 'When Day Is Done'.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: You know I don’t know about you but in meeting a lot of well known musicians you sort of feel that you’re living vicariously, the life that they had. So it’s a thrill for us to be able
to get to know you guys and share some of the — it’s not just musical knowledge, it’s life knowledge I think.
There’s so many things, I’m sorry, so many things come to my mind and I have to say it before I forget it. When we recorded “Daybreak,” here, what was it three years ago?

Yeah. Good. Oh the years that have gone by, oh my goodness, well anyway we did “Daybreak.” You know Paul Whiteman brought that over from Germany. It was called “Madonna.” But in those days that was too religious so they called it “Daybreak.” So we recorded “Daybreak,” and we recorded “When Day Is Done.” But this beautiful lady, who has the brains, she says, “Al, we’re going to open the thing with ‘Daybreak’ and we’ll close it with ‘When Day is Done.” And that’s exactly what we did.
